Wipeout 2097 graphics by The Designers Republic

The PlayStation anti-gravity racing game whose logos, team brands, and packaging by The Designers Republic defined a techno, club-culture future.

Context

Wipeout 2097 was developed by Psygnosis; “the promotional art was designed by Sheffield-based The Designers Republic.” The game and its soundtrack “drew heavily on the ‘future UK’ aesthetic of the 1990s—a style defined by techno-inspired visuals and the rise of electronic music and rave culture.” Wikipedia: Wipeout 2097.

The Designers Republic lists the Wipeout series as a project. The Designers Republic: Wipeout.

Wikipedia says The Designers Republic is sometimes associated with popularizing the Y2K aesthetic. Wikipedia: Y2K aesthetic.

Why it belongs

Wipeout gave the late-1990s future a corporate identity: fictional racing teams with logos and sponsor language, treated like real consumer brands. The coded, branded surface of later Y2K graphics follows from this.

It sits at the start of the period, before translucent plastic and chrome web graphics, so it counts as a precursor here.

Borrow

Invent a small family of brand marks, each with its own color and code, to populate a futuristic interface.
